seoTitle: How to Make Candlesticks Bigger and Bolder on TradingView
metaDescription: Thin candlesticks hard to read? Learn how to enlarge candle bodies, adjust borders, and pick better color contrast on TradingView for clearer charts.
intro: Thin, cramped candlesticks make price action genuinely harder to read, especially once you've layered indicators like a 200 EMA or a moving average on top and the chart gets busy. TradingView's default candle width works fine at a glance, but zoomed out or on a smaller screen it can leave individual candles barely distinguishable from each other. This guide covers where candle sizing and appearance actually live in TradingView's settings, what changes once you widen them, and how to keep the same look consistent across your charts.

steps.heading: Start from the default candle view
steps.body: On a fresh chart at a lower timeframe, TradingView's default candlesticks are noticeably narrow — functional for reading direction and general shape, but each individual candle takes up only a sliver of horizontal space, especially with a watchlist docked on the side eating into your chart width. This is the baseline most people are trying to fix: candles that are technically readable but require squinting or zooming in constantly during active analysis.

image.caption: A 1-minute chart with TradingView's default candle width — each candle is legible, but thin enough that fast price action is easy to skim over.

steps.heading: Open the chart Settings panel
steps.body: Right-click the chart or use the gear icon in the toolbar to open Settings, then go to the Canvas tab. This is where chart-wide visual controls live — background style, grid lines, pane separators, the crosshair's appearance, watermark visibility, and the scale text size and color — all grouped under headings like Chart basic styles, Scales, and Buttons. Candle-specific styling (body, border, and wick colors and widths) lives in this same settings dialog, just under a separate Candles heading you'll find alongside these canvas-wide options.

image.caption: The Settings panel's Canvas tab, covering chart-wide appearance — background, grid lines, crosshair style, and scale text — alongside the candle styling options.

steps.heading: Increase candle body width and border thickness
steps.body: Within the candle styling options, widening the body setting is what actually makes each candlestick occupy more horizontal space and read as bolder at a glance. Pushing the border thickness up alongside it helps candles stand out distinctly from their neighbors rather than blurring together, which matters most at lower timeframes where dozens of candles are packed into the same viewport. There's a balance point — too wide and you're seeing fewer candles per screen, which can hide the broader trend context you'd otherwise catch by zooming out.

steps.heading: Compare the result against your original view
steps.body: After widening the body and border settings, the same price action reads completely differently — each candle is a clearly separated block of color rather than a thin sliver, and bullish versus bearish direction is obvious without leaning in toward the screen. This is the practical test of whether you've gone far enough: if you can tell direction and relative size at a normal viewing distance without zooming, the width is doing its job.

image.caption: The same chart after widening candle bodies and borders — each candle now reads as a distinct, bold block rather than a thin line.

steps.heading: Pick contrast-friendly colors for your theme
steps.body: Wider candles make color contrast matter more, not less, since a poorly chosen bullish or bearish color is now covering more pixels. On a dark theme, brighter greens and reds read better than the muted defaults; on a light theme, slightly deeper, more saturated tones tend to hold up against the white background without washing out. Set these separately for whichever theme you actually trade in most, since a color that looks fine in daylight testing can be much harder to read once you switch to a night theme.

steps.heading: Save the look as a template for consistency
steps.body: Once you're happy with the width, border, and color combination, use the Template option at the bottom of the Settings panel to save it, so every new chart you open inherits the same bold candle styling instead of reverting to TradingView's defaults. If you also trade from the mobile app, repeat the same adjustments there — the settings aren't shared automatically between desktop and mobile, though the underlying options (body width, border, color) are the same on both.

faq.question: Why do my candlesticks look too thin on TradingView?
faq.answer: Thin candles are simply TradingView's default sizing, especially noticeable at lower timeframes — they can be widened through the Candles section of the chart's Settings panel.

faq.question: Does making candles bigger affect indicator accuracy?
faq.answer: No. Enlarging candlesticks is purely a visual adjustment — it makes price action easier to read but has no effect on how indicators like RSI, MACD, or moving averages are calculated.

faq.question: Can I make candles bigger on the TradingView mobile app?
faq.answer: Yes, similar candlestick width and color options are available in the mobile app, though you'll need to set them up separately since settings aren't shared automatically between desktop and mobile.

faq.question: What color contrast works best for reading candlesticks at night?
faq.answer: Brighter, higher-saturation colors against a dark chart background tend to be easier to distinguish than the muted defaults — worth adjusting separately from whatever you use on a light theme.

faq.question: Where exactly do I change candle width in TradingView?
faq.answer: Open Settings from the chart, and look for the Candles section alongside the Canvas tab — body width, border thickness, and colors are all controlled from there.
